title: Michael Jordan
summary: This document is a comprehensive Wikipedia-style biographical article about Michael Jordan, the legendary American basketball player and businessman. The article begins with an overview of his life and career, noting his status as one of the most influential sports figures in history, his six NBA championships with the Chicago Bulls, and his $4.3 billion net worth. It then covers his early life in Brooklyn and Wilmington, North Carolina, including being cut from his high school varsity team before becoming a McDonald's All-American. The college career section details his time at the University of North Carolina, where he hit the game-winning shot in the 1982 NCAA Championship. The extensive professional career section chronicles his NBA journey chronologically: his early years with the Bulls (1984–1987), struggles against the Detroit Pistons (1987–1990), his first three-peat of championships (1991–1993), his surprising first retirement to play Minor League Baseball following his father's murder, his 1995 comeback, his second three-peat (1996–1998) including the famous "Flu Game" and 1998 Finals-winning shot, his second retirement, and final seasons with the Washington Wizards (2001–2003). Additional sections cover his undefeated national team career including the 1992 "Dream Team" Olympic gold; his player profile highlighting his clutch performance, competitiveness, and versatile skills; his legacy as widely considered the greatest basketball player of all time, including his records, cultural impact, and the "Crying Jordan" meme; a comprehensive list of awards and honors spanning NBA, Olympic, NCAA, and Hall of Fame recognition; his post-retirement business ventures including ownership of the Charlotte Bobcats/Hornets and co-founding 23XI Racing in NASCAR; his personal life covering marriages, divorces, gambling controversies, and political stances; and his media and business empire, including the iconic Air Jordan brand with Nike, endorsements, philanthropic efforts, film appearances like Space Jam and The Last Dance documentary, and published books.
